summary: Follow-up plan for layers L1–L4 of Arithmetic Iwasawa theory, continuing the accepted I.8 packet, whose 26 L1–L4 nodes keep their ids. It discharges every remaining item of that packet's coverage: the Iwasawa modules X and Y get a definition with API and tests, RJW's principal closures and sequence (13-1) are identified with I.2's global–local sequence and with Coleman's real principal towers, and limit exactness and topological Nakayama are bound to the merged PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §5.2. L2 adds ℤ_p-extensions, their ramification theorem, the tower invariants μ, λ, ν, the discharge of the growth cutoff, coinvariant evaluation with both twist conventions, and descent of μ = 0 along finite extensions. L3 proves the one-prime hypotheses for the real cyclotomic tower, the Vandiver/plus-part/regularity comparison, and one normalisation of ζ_p. L4 moves the Leopoldt defect to I.2, extends Baker–Brumer to arbitrary algebraic numbers, and closes the parent's gap G3 except at the dyadic plus part: Sinnott's Γ-transform proof gives analytic μ = 0 at every p, the relative class number formula gives μ^- = 0 at every p, and Leopoldt's mirror inequality gives μ^+ = 0 for p odd. It also plans Washington's theorem on the prime-to-p part of class numbers.

nodes.title: The Iwasawa modules X and Y of an arithmetic tower
nodes.statement: Let k be a number field inside a fixed algebraic closure, p a prime, and F_∞/k a Galois extension that is the increasing union of finite Galois extensions F_n/k and contains the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension of F_1; write G = Gal(F_∞/k). Using I.2's maximal abelian pro-p extensions, put M(F) = M_S(F) with S the places above p and ∞ (the p-ramified extension, with I.2's archimedean convention) and L(F) = M_∅(F) (the unramified one), for F equal to F_∞ or to a layer F_n. Define X(F_∞) = Gal(M(F_∞)/F_∞) and Y(F_∞) = Gal(L(F_∞)/F_∞), and at finite level X_n = Gal(M(F_n)/F_n) and Y_n = Gal(L(F_n)/F_n) ≅ Cl(F_n) ⊗ ℤ_p. X(F_∞) and Y(F_∞) are compact ℤ_p⟦G⟧-modules for the conjugation action of the parent L1/conjugation-completed-action. The notation is RJW's: X is p-ramified and Y unramified. I.2 and Sharifi write X (or X_∞) for the unramified module and 𝔛 for the p-ramified one, and Greither writes Y for the p-ramified module; every comparison names the convention it uses. RJW's main case is k = ℚ, F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^n}) for n ≥ 1, p odd, together with the real tower F_n^+.
hypotheses: p is a prime; for p = 2 the archimedean places in S follow I.2's convention (real places may ramify only if listed).
F_∞ ⊇ F_1 is Galois over k and contains the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension of F_1, so F_∞/F_n is abelian pro-p and unramified outside p for n ≥ 1 in RJW's case.
proofSteps: Specialise I.2/maximal-abelian-pro-p-extensions at E = F_∞ and at E = F_n; no second construction of a maximal extension is made.
Transport the conjugation action and its completed extension from the parent node L1/conjugation-completed-action.
Identify Y_n with the p-part of the class group by I.2/class-field-identification and Y(F_∞) with lim Y_n along norms; in I.2's letters Y is X(F_∞) and X is 𝔛_S(F_∞).

nodes.title: RJW's principal unit closures and I.2's global–local sequence
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, n ≥ 1, K = F_n^+ = ℚ(μ_{p^n})^+ and 𝔭 its unique prime above p, with completion K_𝔭 of residue field 𝔽_p. Then: (a) I.2's semilocal principal units U(K) are U^+_{n,1} = 1 + 𝔪_𝔭; (b) I.2's completed global units Ē(K), the image of O_K^× ⊗ ℤ_p in U(K), equal RJW's E^+_{n,1} = (closure of O_K^× in O_𝔭^×) ∩ U^+_{n,1}; (c) the same holds with O_K^× replaced by the cyclotomic units D_n^+, giving C^+_{n,1}; (d) I.2/global-local-unit-sequence (a) at K, with S the places above p and ∞, is RJW's sequence (13-1) 0 → E^+_{n,1} → U^+_{n,1} → Gal(M^+_n/L^+_n) → 0 followed by Gal(M_n^+/F_n^+) → Y_n^+ → 0, and these identifications commute with norms and with the action of Gal(F_n^+/ℚ).
hypotheses: p odd; one prime above p in F_n^+, totally ramified, with residue field 𝔽_p; no real-place sign factor occurs for odd p.
proofSteps: Every element u of O_𝔭^× factors uniquely as ω(u)·⟨u⟩ with ω(u) a (p−1)-th root of unity and ⟨u⟩ ∈ U^+_{n,1}; ⟨u⟩ = (u^{p−1})^{1/(p−1)}, the root taken in the pro-p group U^+_{n,1}.
The closure C of a subgroup V ⊆ O_𝔭^× meets U^+_{n,1} in a closed subgroup of a pro-p group, hence a ℤ_p-module; so ⟨C⟩ ⊆ C ∩ U^+_{n,1} ⊆ ⟨C⟩, and ⟨C⟩ is the image of V ⊗ ℤ_p.
Apply this to V = O_K^× and to V = D_n^+; compare with I.2/semilocal-principal-units, whose map kills prime-to-p roots of unity by passing to the pro-p completion.
Read off (13-1) from I.2/global-local-unit-sequence (a) and Galois theory of L_n^+ ⊆ M_n^+, and check norm and Galois compatibility on generators.

nodes.title: The L1 unit towers are Coleman's real principal towers
nodes.statement: Let p be odd. Under ColemanPowerSeries' root-compatible embedding at Coleman level m = n − 1 (Coleman's level m is the field ℚ_p(ζ_{p^{m+1}}), RJW's F_n with n = m + 1), the completion of F_n^+ at its prime above p is identified with Coleman's real local field, and: U^+_{n,1} corresponds to the residue-one part of Coleman's real local units; the L1 closure C̄^+_n (closure of the principal real cyclotomic units D^+_n ∩ U^+_{n,1}) corresponds to Coleman's C^+_{m,1} (closure of the real cyclotomic units intersected with principal units); the limits C_∞^+ ⊆ U_∞^+ correspond to Coleman's real principal cyclotomic limit C_{∞,1}^+ ⊆ U_{∞,1}^+, by a topological ℤ_p⟦G^+⟧-linear isomorphism.
hypotheses: p odd; G^+ = Gal(ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+/ℚ) acts on both sides through the cyclotomic character.
proofSteps: Check that the global embedding, the norms and complex conjugation match level by level (ColemanPowerSeries:L4/global-to-local-cyclotomic-embedding).

Closure-then-intersection equals intersection-then-closure for the cyclotomic units by the Teichmüller projection of L1/global-local-dictionary (Coleman intersects after closing; RJW closes after intersecting).
Pass to inverse limits; equivariance for G^+ is checked on Dirac elements and extended by continuity (Coleman's completed action adapter).

The proof uses that every term is a compact Hausdorff group and every map continuous; the transition maps of E^+_{n,1} need not be surjective.

proofSteps: Apply the compact inverse-system exactness of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §5.2 (built on Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups layer 9) to each short exact sequence.
Identify lim Gal(M_n^+/F_n^+) with X_∞^+ and lim Y_n^+ with Y_∞^+ by L1/rjw-iwasawa-modules (maximal_union) and the parent comparison.

nodes.title: Iwasawa's rank theorem for the p-ramified module
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, F_∞ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞}), Γ = Gal(F_∞/ℚ(μ_p)) and Λ = ℤ_p⟦Γ⟧. Then X(F_∞) (RJW's letter; I.2's 𝔛_S(F_∞)) is a finitely generated Λ-module of rank r_2(ℚ(μ_p)) = (p−1)/2; its plus part X(F_∞)^+ = X^+(F_∞^+) is Λ-torsion, so the rank is carried by the minus part; and Y(F_∞) is Λ-torsion. More generally, for any ℤ_p-extension satisfying weak Leopoldt, rank_Λ X = r_2 of the base field.
hypotheses: p odd; ^± are the eigenspaces of complex conjugation, which are direct summands because 2 is invertible.
proofSteps: Weak Leopoldt holds for cyclotomic ℤ_p-extensions (I.2/weak-leopoldt, stated there for 𝔛_S), so rank_Λ X = r_2(ℚ(μ_p)) (Sharifi Theorem 3.3.3: compare ℤ_p-ranks of the Γ_n-coinvariants with those of X_n).

Plus part: in the limit sequence of L1/compact-limit-exactness-application, U_∞^+ has Λ-rank (p−1)/2 and contains C_∞^+, whose quotient U_∞^+/C_∞^+ ≅ Λ(G^+)/I(G^+)ζ_p is torsion (Coleman); E^+_∞/C^+_∞ is a submodule and Gal(M^+/L^+) a quotient of U^+/C^+, both torsion, and Y^+ is torsion by L2.
Y(F_∞) is torsion by the one-prime control and the finiteness of all Y_n (parent L2/class-module-finiteness-torsion with L2/real-cyclotomic-one-prime-tower).

nodes.title: Ray class limits, split-prime quotients and ambiguous classes
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, p a prime and F_∞/F its cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension with Γ = Gal(F_∞/F) and generator γ, T = γ − 1. (a) For each n, Gal(M(F_n)/F_n) is the inverse limit over ν of the p-parts of the ray class groups of F_n of conductor p^ν (with I.2's archimedean convention), and restriction gives an exact sequence 0 → X(F_∞)_{Γ_n} → Gal(M(F_n)/F_n) → Γ_n → 0, Γ_n = Γ^{p^n}. (b) If F is totally real and Leopoldt holds for F (for instance F abelian, by L4), then X(F_∞)_Γ is finite and is isomorphic to the torsion subgroup of Gal(M(F)/F); Greither's A′(F) ≅ X/TX must be read with A′(F) the torsion part, the free ℤ_p summand mapping onto Γ. (c) With L′(F_∞) ⊆ L(F_∞) the maximal subextension in which the primes above p split completely, Gal(L′(F_∞)/F_∞) ≅ Y(F_∞)/D_∞, where D_∞ is the closed submodule generated by the decomposition groups of the finitely many primes above p. (d) For a cyclic extension E/F with group G and inertia groups I_v, Sharifi's nine-term sequence relates ker j_{E/F}, H^1(G, O_E^×), the ambiguous ideal classes Cl_E^G, O_F^×/N O_E^×, ker Σ and coker Σ for Σ: ⊕ I_v → G; Chevalley's ambiguous class number formula #Cl_E^G = h_F·∏_v e_v /([E:F]·[O_F^× : O_F^× ∩ N_{E/F}E^×]) follows.
hypotheses: For (b), F totally real and δ(F, p) = 0; for (d), E/F cyclic of number fields.
proofSteps: (a) is I.2/class-field-identification (c) at the layer F_n together with Galois theory of F_∞ ⊆ M(F_n); the quotient Γ_n is ℤ_p-free, so the sequence splits as ℤ_p-modules.
(b) Leopoldt gives rank_{ℤ_p} Gal(M(F)/F) = 1 + r_2(F) = 1 for F totally real, so X(F_∞)_Γ has rank 0, is finite, and is the torsion of a split extension by ℤ_p.
(c) is I.2/class-field-identification (b) with S the primes above p (X′_S), Galois theory and finiteness of the set of primes of F_∞ above p (I.1/tower-ramification).

(d) Sharifi Theorem 1.3.16 gives the exact sequence; the ambiguous class number formula is its order count, using the Herbrand quotient of units for cyclic groups, the norm index theorem (ClassFieldTheory layer 12) and Hasse's norm theorem for cyclic extensions (layer 13).

nodes.title: ℤ_p-extensions and their layers
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field inside a fixed algebraic closure and p a prime. A ℤ_p-extension of F is a Galois extension F_∞/F with a continuous group isomorphism Gal(F_∞/F) ≅ ℤ_p for the Krull topology. Its n-th layer F_n is the fixed field of Γ^{p^n}, Γ = Gal(F_∞/F); F_n is the unique subextension of degree p^n, F_0 = F, and F_∞ = ⋃ F_n. Write Γ_n = Gal(F_∞/F_n) = Γ^{p^n}. A topological generator γ gives Λ = ℤ_p⟦Γ⟧ ≅ ℤ_p⟦T⟧, T ↦ γ − 1 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §4.5), with ω_n = (1+T)^{p^n} − 1 = γ^{p^n} − 1 and ν_{n,m} = ω_n/ω_m for n ≥ m.
hypotheses: Topological isomorphism with ℤ_p, not an abstract one; the layers are indexed so that F_0 = F.
proofSteps: Closed subgroups of ℤ_p are 0 and p^nℤ_p, so the Galois correspondence of infinite Galois theory (Mathlib) lists the intermediate fields.
The Iwasawa coordinate and the cyclotomic polynomials ω_n are those of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras layer 4; I.1 specialises them to the cyclotomic case.

nodes.title: Ramification in a ℤ_p-extension
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be a ℤ_p-extension of a number field. (a) Every prime not above p is unramified in F_∞/F, and every archimedean place splits completely. (b) At least one prime above p ramifies. (c) There is m ≥ 0 such that every prime of F_m ramified in F_∞/F_m is totally ramified in F_∞/F_m; for every ramified prime v of F its inertia group I_v ⊆ Γ is open.
hypotheses: Number field F; p any prime.
proofSteps: (a) For v ∤ p, the image of the local units in the pro-p abelianisation is finite (principal units at v are pro-ℓ, ℓ ≠ p, and the residue units are finite), so I_v is a finite subgroup of ℤ_p, hence trivial; real places: Γ has no element of order 2.
(b) If no prime ramified, F_∞ would lie in the Hilbert class field tower's first abelian layer of F, which is finite (finiteness of the class group via ClassFieldTheory layer 12).
(c) Each I_v for v | p is a nonzero closed subgroup, hence equal to Γ^{p^{m_v}}; take m = max m_v over the finitely many v | p.

nodes.title: Arithmetic towers satisfy the growth and Nakayama hypotheses
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be a ℤ_p-extension and m as in L2/zp-extension-ramification, and H_m = ker(Y_∞ → Cl(F_m) ⊗ ℤ_p). Then H_m/ν_{n,m}H_m is finite for every n ≥ m, with #Cl(F_n)⊗ℤ_p = #Cl(F_m)⊗ℤ_p · #(H_m/ν_{n,m}H_m); hence the finiteness hypothesis of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras' growth theorem (finiteness of M/ν_{n,n₀}M for n ≥ n₀) holds for M = H_m with n₀ = m, and the cyclotomic cutoff of H_m is at most m − 1. In the one-prime totally ramified case, Y_∞/ω_nY_∞ ≅ Cl(F_n) ⊗ ℤ_p is finite for all n, so the cutoff of Y_∞ is −1. Y_∞ and H_m are compact, so topological Nakayama applies to them.
hypotheses: m beyond eventual total ramification; Y_∞ with the inverse-limit topology.
proofSteps: The norm relation H_n = ν_{n,m}H_m and the order formula are the parent L2/inertia-kernel-norm-relation; finiteness of class groups gives finiteness.
The growth theorem of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §4.7 is stated with ν_{n,n₀} and hypothesis hfin; the arithmetic H_m with n₀ = m discharges it.
Compactness: Y_∞ is an inverse limit of finite groups; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §5.2 states Nakayama for compact modules.

nodes.title: Coinvariant orders and characteristic series at finite evaluation points
nodes.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite unramified extension of ℚ_p (for instance O_χ, generated by the values of a character of order prime to p), Λ_O = O⟦T⟧ with T = γ − 1, and M a finitely generated torsion Λ_O-module with characteristic ideal (f). If M_Γ = M/TM is finite, then M^Γ = M[T] is finite and #M_Γ = #(O/f(0)O) · #M^Γ; in particular #M_Γ = p^{[O:ℤ_p]·v_p(f(0))} when M^Γ = 0. For n ∈ ℤ and the twist M(n) (γ acting by κ(γ)^nγ), char(M(n)) is generated by f(κ(γ)^{−n}(1+T) − 1), so #M(n)_Γ/#M(n)^Γ = #(O/f(κ(γ)^{−n} − 1)O) when finite. Two dual conventions are kept apart: (i) contragredient: the Pontryagin dual of the discrete module Hom_cts(X, ℚ_p/ℤ_p(n)) is X(−n) (γ acting by κ(γ)^{−n}γ) with series f(κ(γ)^n(1+T) − 1), evaluated at κ(γ)^n − 1; (ii) Kolster's covariant convention (γφ)(x) = φ(γx): dualising 𝒯 ⊗ A multiplies the action by u = κ(γ), giving f(u^{−1}(1+T) − 1) evaluated at u^{−1} − 1. Each evaluation formula requires the corresponding value to be nonzero.
hypotheses: O unramified over ℤ_p (so #O/p^aO = p^{[O:ℤ_p]a}); M finitely generated torsion; the value f(·) at the evaluation point is nonzero.
proofSteps: Apply the Euler quotient at depth n = 0 of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §4.7: #M_{Γ}/#M^{Γ} = q^{μ}·#(O/Res(F_M, T)) = #(O/f(0)O), since Res(F_M, T) = ±F_M(0) and f = ϖ^μ F_M up to a unit.
Twists: I.1/iwasawa-algebra-coordinate gives char(M ⊗ ℤ_p(n)) = Tw_{−n}(char M), and Tw_{−n} sends T to κ(γ)^{−n}(1+T) − 1.

Duals: the double dual returns the compact module, so the contragredient convention gives the twist X(−n); in Kolster's covariant convention the action is multiplied by u = κ(γ), the twist by −1 in the same formula. The involution ι of I.1 enters only when the dual of a compact module itself is compared with the module.

nodes.title: μ-vanishing descends along finite extensions
nodes.statement: Let F_∞/F be a ℤ_p-extension, F′/F a finite extension and F′_∞ = F′F_∞, a ℤ_p-extension of F′ (L2/zp-extension). For every n the norm Cl(F′F_n) → Cl(F_n) has cokernel isomorphic to Gal((F′F_n ∩ H(F_n))/F_n), of order dividing [F′:F], where H(F_n) is the Hilbert class field. Hence r_p(Cl(F_n)) ≤ r_p(Cl(F′F_n)) + v_p([F′:F]), and μ(F′_∞/F′) = 0 implies μ(F_∞/F) = 0.
hypotheses: F′/F finite; F′F_n is a layer of F′_∞/F′ up to a bounded shift of index.
proofSteps: Artin reciprocity is compatible with norms (ClassFieldTheory layer 13, artinMap_norm): the image of the norm in Gal(H(F_n)/F_n) is Gal(H(F_n)/H(F_n) ∩ F′F_n).
The cokernel has order dividing [F′F_n : F_n] ≤ [F′ : F]; the p-rank of a quotient exceeds the p-rank of the source by at most the p-rank of the cokernel.
Bounded p-ranks for F′_∞ give bounded p-ranks for F_∞, and the parent L2/bounded-p-rank-mu-zero converts this into μ = 0.

nodes.title: The real cyclotomic tower is a one-prime totally ramified ℤ_p-extension
nodes.statement: Let p be odd and F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^n}) (n ≥ 1, RJW's indexing). Then F_∞^+/F_1^+ and F_∞/F_1 are the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extensions of F_1^+ = ℚ(μ_p)^+ and F_1 = ℚ(μ_p), with ℤ_p-layer j equal to F_{j+1}^+, resp. F_{j+1}. Each of F_1^+, F_1 has a unique prime above p; it is totally ramified in the whole tower, no other finite prime ramifies, and the real places of F_1^+ split completely. Hence the hypotheses of the parent L2/one-prime-inertia-control hold, and Y_n^+ ≅ (Y_∞^+)_{Γ^+_{n−1}} with Γ^+_{n−1} = Gal(F_∞^+/F_n^+).
hypotheses: p odd; the shift between the cyclotomic exponent n and the ℤ_p-layer j = n − 1 is explicit.
proofSteps: Gal(ℚ(μ_{p^∞})/ℚ) ≅ ℤ_p^× = μ_{p−1} × (1 + pℤ_p) by the cyclotomic character; F_1 is the fixed field of 1 + pℤ_p and F_∞/F_1 has group 1 + pℤ_p ≅ ℤ_p.
(p) = (1 − ζ_{p^n})^{φ(p^n)} in ℚ(μ_{p^n}), so p is totally ramified (ColemanPowerSeries' local cyclotomic Eisenstein criterion); hence so is its unique prime in F_1 and F_1^+.
Primes ℓ ≠ p are unramified (I.1/tower-ramification (a)); complex conjugation lies in the torsion of ℤ_p^×, so real places of F_1^+ split.
Read RJW Proposition 13.15 as the parent one-prime control at layer j = n − 1.

nodes.title: Vandiver's condition through the tower and its difference from regularity
nodes.statement: Let p be odd and F_n = ℚ(μ_{p^n}). The following are equivalent: (i) Vandiver(p), i.e. p ∤ h(ℚ(μ_p)^+); (ii) Cl(F_n^+) ⊗ ℤ_p = 0 for every n ≥ 1; (iii) the plus part (Cl(F_n) ⊗ ℤ_p)^+ (fixed by complex conjugation) vanishes for every n ≥ 1; (iv) Y_∞^+ = 0. Regularity of p (p ∤ h(ℚ(μ_p))) implies these but is strictly stronger: p = 37 is irregular (37 divides the numerator of B_32) and satisfies Vandiver(37).
hypotheses: p odd; plus parts are taken in the p-part, where 1 + c and 1 − c are orthogonal idempotents up to the unit 2.
proofSteps: (i) ⇒ (ii), (iv): the parent L3/vandiver-unramified-vanishing; (ii) ⇒ (i) is the case n = 1.
(ii) ⇔ (iii): for p odd the extension map Cl(F_n^+) ⊗ ℤ_p → Cl(F_n) ⊗ ℤ_p is injective (norm after extension is multiplication by 2) and its image is the plus part ((1 + c)/2 is the projector).
(iv) ⇒ (ii): one-prime control (L2/real-cyclotomic-one-prime-tower) identifies Y_n^+ with coinvariants of Y_∞^+.
Regularity ⇒ Vandiver since h^+ divides h; the example p = 37 separates them.

nodes.title: One normalisation of ζ_p for the Vandiver isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, G^+ = Gal(ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+/ℚ) ≅ ℤ_p^×/{±1} by the cyclotomic character, and I(G^+) its augmentation ideal. The ideal I(G^+)ζ_p of RJW Theorems 11.9 and 13.8 equals ColemanPowerSeries' I(G^+)ζ_p^+ (the image of the real principal cyclotomic limit under the Coleman map) and the even part of the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure of DirichletPadicLFunctions L1 (I.3's dictionary), as ideals of Λ(G^+). Under the decomposition Λ(G^+) ≅ ⊕_χ O_χ⟦T⟧ over even characters χ of Δ = Gal(ℚ(μ_p)/ℚ), the χ ≠ 1 component of I(G^+)ζ_p is generated by f_χ with f_χ(u^s − 1) = L_p(χ, s) (I.3's Iwasawa power series), and the χ = 1 component by the pole-cleared trivial branch. Through L1/coleman-real-closure-comparison, the parent's isomorphism X_∞^+ ≅ U_∞^+/C_∞^+ ≅ Λ(G^+)/I(G^+)ζ_p is Coleman's quotient map read at RJW's levels.
hypotheses: p odd; u = κ(γ) for the chosen generator γ of 1 + pℤ_p; character components use their unramified coefficient rings.
proofSteps: Coleman's real image theorem gives I(G^+)ζ_p^+ with his pseudo-measure; I.3/kubota-leopoldt-stickelberger-dictionary identifies it with the Kubota–Leopoldt pseudo-measure and Iwasawa's series.
Compare the augmentation factors: on χ ≠ 1 the augmentation ideal is the unit ideal, on χ = 1 it is (T).
Compose with the root-indexing shift of L1/coleman-real-closure-comparison.

nodes.title: Abelian Leopoldt in I.2's form, and the logarithmic defect
nodes.statement: For a number field E and prime p, let δ(E, p) = rank_{ℤ_p} ker(ι_E: O_E^× ⊗ ℤ_p → ∏_{v|p} U^1(E_v)) be I.2's Leopoldt defect and δ_log(E, p) = dim_{ℚ_p} ker(ℓ_{E,p}) the logarithmic defect of the parent L4/leopoldt-defect, ℓ_{E,p} = (log_p ∘ ι_E) ⊗ ℚ_p. Then δ_log = δ. Consequently the parent L4/abelian-leopoldt states I.2's LeopoldtConjecture(E, p) for every finite abelian E/ℚ and every p, and the principal closure of global units of F_n^+ has ℤ_p-rank [F_n^+:ℚ] − 1. The parent L4/leopoldt-defect is a characterisation of I.2's definition, not a second definition.

proofSteps: On U^1(E_v), log_p has kernel the p-power roots of unity of E_v, a finite group; so ker(log_p ∘ ι_E) contains ker ι_E with finite index after tensoring with ℚ_p.
Hence ker(ℓ_{E,p}) = ker(ι_E) ⊗ ℚ_p and the dimensions agree; rank formulas follow from I.2's leopoldtDefect_eq.

nodes.title: Baker–Brumer for arbitrary algebraic numbers with Iwasawa's logarithm
nodes.statement: Fix an embedding of ℚ̄ into ℂ_p and let log_p be Iwasawa's logarithm on ℂ_p^× (log_p p = 0). (a) For α ∈ ℚ̄^×, log_p α = 0 iff α^N = ζ·p^k for some N ≥ 1, k ∈ ℤ and root of unity ζ. (b) For α_1, …, α_r ∈ ℚ̄^×, if log_p α_1, …, log_p α_r are linearly independent over ℚ, they are linearly independent over ℚ̄. (c) Multiplicative reduction: the ℚ-span of the log_p α_i equals the ℚ-span of log_p β_i, where α_i^N = p^{k_i}β_i with β_i algebraic p-adic units. The statement holds for p = 2. It does not by itself show that a given character projection of a vector of logarithms is nonzero.
hypotheses: Iwasawa's branch: log_p(p) = 0, log_p(ζ) = 0 for roots of unity, log_p(xy) = log_p x + log_p y.
proofSteps: For α algebraic, v_p(α) ∈ (1/e)ℤ; choose N with N·v_p(α_i) ∈ ℤ for all i, put k_i = N·v_p(α_i) and β_i = α_i^N p^{−k_i}, an algebraic p-adic unit; then log_p α_i = log_p(β_i)/N.
(a) For a p-adic unit β, log_p β = 0 iff β is a root of unity (the kernel of log_p on the units of ℂ_p is the torsion subgroup); combine with the first step.
(b) Apply the parent L4/baker-brumer-independence to β_1, …, β_r, whose logarithms are Q-independent iff those of the α_i are.

nodes.title: The Γ-transform of a measure
nodes.statement: Let o be the ring of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p with uniformiser π, and α an o-valued measure on ℤ_p. Write ℤ_p^× = V × U with V the roots of unity in ℤ_p (μ_{p−1} for p odd, {±1} for p = 2) and U = 1 + qℤ_p (q = p or 4), x = ω(x)⟨x⟩, and fix a topological generator u of U. The Γ-transform of α is Γ_α(s) = ∫_{ℤ_p^×} ⟨x⟩^s dα(x) for s ∈ ℤ_p. It is an Iwasawa function: Γ_α(s) = G_α(u^s − 1) with G_α ∈ o⟦T⟧ the Amice transform of the pushforward to ℤ_p, through y ↦ u^y, of the restriction to U of β = Σ_{η∈V} α∘η. Define μ(Γ_α) = μ(G_α), the least π-adic valuation of a coefficient.
hypotheses: o-valued measures on ℤ_p are identified with o⟦T⟧ by the Amice transform (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras layer 2); Sinnott writes T for 1 + T.
proofSteps: Restriction to an open compact subset, multiplicative translation α ↦ α∘η and pushforward along the homeomorphism ℤ_p ≅ U are PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras' operations.
The integral splits over the cosets ηU; ⟨ηx⟩ = ⟨x⟩ gives the formula with β.

acceptance: μ(Γ_α) does not depend on the choice of u: changing u is a substitution T ↦ (1+T)^c − 1 with c ∈ ℤ_p^×.

nodes.title: Sinnott's independence results
nodes.statement: (a) Let k be a field, X_1, …, X_n, Z independent indeterminates and Y_1, …, Y_m (m ≥ 1) nontrivial monomials in the X_i that are pairwise multiplicatively independent. If r_1(Y_1) + ⋯ + r_m(Y_m) = 0 with r_j(Z) ∈ k(Z), then every r_j is constant. (b) Let F be a field of characteristic p and, for a ∈ ℤ_p, (1+T)^a = Σ binom(a,n)T^n ∈ F⟦T⟧. If a_1, …, a_n ∈ ℤ_p are linearly independent over ℚ, then (1+T)^{a_1}, …, (1+T)^{a_n} are algebraically independent over F in F((T)). (c) If for each η ∈ V a rational function r_η(Z) ∈ F(Z) is given with Σ_{η∈V} r_η((1+T)^η) = 0 in F((T)), then r_η(Z) + r_{−η}(Z^{−1}) ∈ F for each η.
hypotheses: F of characteristic p; V the roots of unity of ℤ_p; in (a) monomials have integer exponents.
proofSteps: (a) Enlarge k to contain an element t of infinite order; take a minimal nonconstant relation, choose integers b_i killing the exponent vector of Y_1 but not of Y_2, apply X_i ↦ X_i t^{b_i} and subtract to get a shorter relation.

(b) A polynomial relation Σ b_D (1+T)^{d·a} = 0 survives every continuous substitution (1+T) ↦ (1+T)^x, x ∈ ℤ_p; the exponents d·a are distinct, and Artin's independence of characters x ↦ (1+T)^{x·c} kills every b_D.

(c) Choose a ℤ-basis a_1, …, a_n of the additive group generated by V and representatives η_1, …, η_m of V/±1; the (1+T)^{η_j} are pairwise independent monomials in the algebraically independent X_i = (1+T)^{a_i}, and apply (a) to r_{η_j}(Z) + r_{−η_j}(Z^{−1}).

sources.locator: §3, Proposition 3.1, the Lemma and Proposition 3.2, pp. 277–279
sources.match: Proves the independence of rational functions of independent monomials, the algebraic independence of the T^{a_i} and the cancellation for sums over V.

acceptance: For a single a ∉ ℚ, (1+T)^a is transcendental over F(T).
For η and −η the relation r(Z) + r(Z^{−1}) ∈ F is all that can be concluded; it is not r = 0.

nodes.title: Sinnott's μ-theorem for Γ-transforms of rational functions
nodes.statement: Let α be an o-valued measure on ℤ_p whose associated power series is a rational function. Then μ(Γ_α) = μ(α* + α*∘(−1)), where α* is the restriction of α to ℤ_p^× (extended by 0) and μ of a measure is the μ-invariant of its power series. The power series of α* is F(T) − p^{−1}Σ_{ζ^p=1} F(ζ(1+T) − 1), again rational.
hypotheses: Valid for every prime p, including p = 2; o the integers of a finite extension of ℚ_p.
proofSteps: Reduce to α supported on ℤ_p^×, even and not divisible by π (replacing α by α* + α*∘(−1) doubles Γ_α and scaling by π lowers both μ-invariants equally); then μ(2α) = 0 for p odd and 1 for p = 2.

p odd: if G ∈ πo⟦T⟧ then β|_U ∈ πΛ; translating with the rational series F_η of α|_{ηU} (rational by restriction, Sinnott Lemma 1.1) gives Σ_η F_η((1+T)^{η^{−1}} − 1) ≡ 0 mod π, so by L4/sinnott-independence (c) F_η + F_{−η}∘inv ≡ c_η, forcing 2α|_{ηU} ∈ πΛ and contradicting the hypothesis.
p = 2: β = 2α gives G ∈ 2o⟦T⟧; if ½G ≡ 0 mod π then α|_U and α|_{−U} lie in πΛ, again a contradiction.

sources.locator: Lemma 1.1, p. 274; Theorem 1 and its proof, pp. 276–277
sources.match: States and proves μ(Γ_α(s)) = μ(α* + α*∘(−1)) for rational α, with the separate p = 2 argument.

acceptance: For α = δ_1 + δ_{−1}: α* + α*∘(−1) = 2α and Γ_α = 2, so for p = 2 both sides have μ = 1.
Rationality of the power series is essential: the theorem is not claimed for arbitrary measures.

nodes.title: Kubota–Leopoldt L-functions as Γ-transforms of rational measures
nodes.statement: Let θ be an odd primitive Dirichlet character of the first kind (p² ∤ f_θ for p odd, 8 ∤ f_θ for p = 2) with θω nontrivial, valued in o, and c > 1 an integer prime to p·f_θ. Let ε(a) = θ(a) if c ∤ a and θ(a)(1 − c) if c | a, and F(T) = Σ_{a=1}^{f} ε(a)(1+T)^a/(1 − (1+T)^f) for f a multiple of the period of ε. Then F ∈ o⟦T⟧ is rational, it is the power series of a measure α, and Γ_α(s) = (1 − θ(c)c⟨c⟩^s)L_p(−s, θω). With Iwasawa's series g(T, θ) ∈ 2o⟦T⟧, L_p(s, θω) = g(u^s − 1, θ), one has μ(½g(T, θ)) = μ(α*), and α* ≢ 0 mod πΛ.
hypotheses: θ odd, primitive, first kind; θω ≠ 1; c prime to p f_θ; the variable conventions of Sinnott (T ↦ 1 + T) are converted.
proofSteps: Integrality: (1 − (1+T)^{gc})/(1 − (1+T)^g)·F ∈ o[T] because exactly one of a + bg is divisible by c, and that factor is a unit since p ∤ c.
Moments: ∫x^k dα = L(−k, ε) = (1 − θ(c)c^{k+1})L(−k, θ) by the Hurwitz formula; interpolate along k ≡ 0 mod p − 1 to get the Γ-transform formula.
Write the factor 1 − θ(c)c⟨c⟩^s = H(u^s − 1) with μ(H) = 0, so μ(g) = μ(G_α) = μ(Γ_α) = μ(α* + α*∘(−1)) by L4/sinnott-mu-theorem; ε is odd so α∘(−1) = α and the sum is 2α*.
With f divisible by p, (1 − (1+T)^f)·F*(T) = Σ_{p∤a} ε(a)(1+T)^a; as a polynomial in 1 + T its coefficient of (1+T)^1 is ε(1) = 1, so α* is not divisible by π.

sources.locator: §4, formulas (4.1)–(4.5), Proposition 4.1 and the concluding argument, pp. 279–282
sources.match: Writes L_p(s, θω) as a Γ-transform of the rational measure attached to ε, deduces μ(½g) = μ(α*) and shows α* ≢ 0 mod π.

acceptance: The trivial character (θω = 1) is excluded here; its branch has a pole and is treated in L4/analytic-mu-vanishing-dirichlet.
At p = 2 the factor ½ is part of the statement.

nodes.title: Analytic μ-vanishing for Kubota–Leopoldt branches (Ferrero–Washington, Sinnott)
nodes.statement: For every prime p, including p = 2, and every odd primitive Dirichlet character θ of the first kind with θω nontrivial, μ(½g(T, θ)) = 0; equivalently, every Kubota–Leopoldt branch L_p(s, χ), χ = θω even of the first kind and nontrivial, has integral power series of μ-invariant 0 after the factor ½ at p = 2. For the trivial character, the pole-cleared branch (the zeta pseudo-measure times a clearing factor vanishing simply at s = 1) takes at s = 1 the residue 1 − p^{−1} times ±log_p(u), a p-adic unit for p odd and twice a unit for p = 2, so its μ-invariant (after ½ at p = 2) is also 0.
hypotheses: μ is the π-adic content of the integral series in the normalisation of DirichletPadicLFunctions; no main conjecture is used.
proofSteps: Nontrivial branches: L4/kubota-leopoldt-gamma-transform gives μ(½g) = μ(α*) and α* ≢ 0 mod π, so μ = 0.
Trivial branch: the residue of ζ_p at s = 1 is 1 − p^{−1} (RJW Theorem 7.1(ii)); multiply by the pole factor and use v_p(log_p u) = 1 (p odd, u = 1 + p) or 2 (p = 2, u = 5).

sources.locator: Introduction, p. 273, and §4, pp. 279–282
sources.match: Obtains a new proof that μ = 0 for the basic ℤ_p-extension of abelian fields through μ(½g(T, θ)) = 0, for all p.

sources.locator: Theorem 7.1, p. 154

nodes.title: The minus class-group μ-invariant is analytic, at every prime
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, q = p (p odd) or 4 (p = 2), and k an imaginary abelian field containing μ_q whose conductor is not divisible by qp, with cyclotomic ℤ_p-tower k_n and relative class numbers h_n^- = h(k_n)/h(k_n^+). Then v_p(h_n^-) = μ^-p^n + λ^-n + ν^- for n large, with μ^- = Σ_θ μ_p(½g(T, θ)), the sum over the odd characters θ ≠ ω^{−1} of k (all of the first kind), μ_p being the least p-adic valuation (a rational number) of the coefficients; the character θ = ω^{−1} contributes the μ-invariant of the pole-cleared trivial branch, since its factors L_p(0, ψ) for ψ ≠ 1 of the second kind are values of the pseudo-measure away from its pole. By L4/analytic-mu-vanishing-dirichlet, μ^- = 0 for every p. For p odd this is μ(Y_∞^-) = 0; for p = 2, with I.2's norm-kernel minus part A_n^- = ker(N: A(k_n) → A(k_n^+)), #A_n^- = 2^{v_2(h_n^-)} and μ(lim A_n^-) = μ((A_∞^-)^∨) = 0.
hypotheses: k imaginary abelian, μ_q ⊆ k, qp ∤ conductor; the reduction of a general abelian field to this case uses L2/norm-prank-descent.
proofSteps: Relative class number formula h_n^- = Q_n w_n ∏_{χ odd of k_n} (−½B_{1,χ}), with Q_n ∈ {1, 2}; the odd characters of k_n are θψ with ψ of the second kind of conductor dividing qp^n.

Interpolation: for ψ ≠ 1 of the second kind, θψ(p) = 0, so −B_{1,θψ} = L_p(0, θωψ) = g(ζ_ψ − 1, θ) up to the root-of-unity normalisation of ψ, ζ_ψ a primitive p-power root of unity (I.3's dictionary).

The product of g(ζ − 1) over primitive p^n-th roots ζ is Res(g, ω_n)/Res(g, ω_{n−1}); its valuation is μ(g)φ(p^n) + λ(g) for n large (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras §4.7 cyclotomic growth step). w_n contributes only to λ^- and ν^-.

p = 2: the norm Cl(k_n) → Cl(k_n^+) is surjective because k_n/k_n^+ is ramified at the archimedean places and the wide Hilbert class field of k_n^+ is totally real; so #A_n^- is the 2-part of h_n^-, and I.2/iwasawa-finiteness (c) passes to the Pontryagin dual.

sources.locator: §2, the analytic class number formula for h_n^- with Q_n and w_n, p. 88
sources.match: States h_n^- = Q_n w_n ∏_χ ∏_j (−½B_{1,χψ_n^j}) for the cyclotomic tower of an imaginary abelian field with p² ∤ f_χ.

sources.locator: §4, the formula for h_n^- and the definition of μ^-, λ^-, p. 174
sources.match: States the relative class number formula in the tower and that μ = 0 reduces to the minus part.

sources.locator: Proposition 6.2.4, pp. 160–161
sources.match: For ℚ(μ_p), p odd, μ(X_∞^-) > 0 iff some Iwasawa power series is divisible by p.

acceptance: For p odd and k = ℚ(μ_p), μ^- = Σ_{k even, 2 ≤ k ≤ p−3} μ(f_{ω^k}) = 0.
At p = 2 the statement is about the norm-kernel minus part, not about a minus eigenspace (which does not exist).

nodes.title: Leopoldt's mirror inequality and the plus part of μ, for odd p
nodes.statement: Let p be odd and E a CM field containing μ_p. Then r_p(A(E)^+) ≤ r_p(A(E)^-) + 1, where A = Cl ⊗ ℤ_p and ± are the eigenspaces of complex conjugation. Consequently, for the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension E_∞/E, μ(Y_∞) = 0 if and only if μ(Y_∞^-) = 0.
hypotheses: p odd, μ_p ⊆ E, E CM; the dyadic analogue (E ⊇ μ_4) is not established here (gap G-L4-DYADIC-MIRROR).
proofSteps: Apply Sharifi Theorem 4.4.2 with F = E^+ and χ = ω|_{G_F}, which is the sign character of E/E^+: its first inequality with δ_χ ≤ 1 gives r_p(A^+) − 1 ≤ r_p(A^-).

Tower: μ(Y^-) = 0 gives bounded p-ranks of (Y_∞^-)_{Γ_n} (Sharifi Proposition 2.4.10), the norms Y^-_∞ → A_n^- are onto (Sharifi Proposition 3.4.1), so r_p(A_n^-) is bounded, hence r_p(A_n^+) is bounded, and the coinvariants of Y_∞^+ differ from A_n^+ by a module of p-rank at most the number of ramified primes minus one; apply Proposition 2.4.10 again.
μ(Y_∞) = μ(Y_∞^+) + μ(Y_∞^-) because Y_∞ = Y_∞^+ ⊕ Y_∞^- for p odd.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.4.2 (Leopoldt's Spiegelungssatz) and its proof, pp. 111–113; Proposition 3.4.3, p. 91; Proposition 2.4.10, p. 58
sources.match: Proves the eigenspace mirror inequality for p odd and deduces μ(X_∞) = 0 iff μ(X_∞^-) = 0 when μ_p ⊆ F.
Records μ^+ ≤ μ^- and λ^+ ≤ λ^- for k containing the 2p-th roots of unity, citing Ferrero and Washington.

acceptance: For E = ℚ(μ_p): r_p(A^+) ≤ r_p(A^-) + 1; Vandiver's condition A^+ = 0 is not implied.
The inequality is for p-ranks, not orders; the plus order can be larger than the minus order only within the rank bound.

nodes.title: The integral-basis and sign arrangement for torsion roots
nodes.statement: Let p be odd, R = (p−1)/2, r = φ(p−1), η_1 a primitive (p−1)-th root of unity in ℤ_p and η_j = η_1^j. Then η_1, …, η_r is a ℤ-basis of ℤ[η_1]. If r < R, after replacing some of η_1, …, η_R by their negatives (the set still represents μ_{p−1}/±1) and renumbering the basis, there is j_0 > r such that, writing η_j = Σ_{i≤r} a_{ji}η_i: every a_{j0 i} ≥ 0, a_{j0 1} > 0 and some other a_{j0 i} > 0 (η_{j0}/η_1 ∉ ℤ), and the first nonzero coefficient of every η_j is positive. Then for every m ≥ 1 there are ℚ-linearly independent positive reals x_1, …, x_r such that x_j := Σ_i a_{ji}x_i satisfies 0 < x_j < p^{−m} for j ≠ j_0 and p^{−m} < x_{j0} < 2p^{−m}. If r = R (p a Fermat prime) take j_0 = 1 and choose the x_j directly.
hypotheses: p odd; ℤ[η_1] is the ring of integers of ℚ(η_1), of rank r = φ(p−1).
proofSteps: The powers 1, η_1, …, η_1^{r−1} form a ℤ-basis of the cyclotomic integers ℤ[η_1]; so do η_1, …, η_r (multiply by the unit η_1).

Order η_{r+1}, …, η_R lexicographically by the absolute values of their coefficients and take η_{j0} maximal; change the signs of basis elements so that the coefficients of η_{j0} are nonnegative, and then the signs of the other dependent roots so that their first nonzero coefficient is positive.

Take x_1 = 1 ≫ x_2 ≫ ⋯ ≫ x_r > 0, ℚ-independent, so that the first nonzero term dominates each sum: all x_j > 0, and x_j < x_{j0} for j ≠ j0 because η_{j0} is lexicographically maximal with two positive coefficients; multiply all x_i by one real c to place x_{j0} in (p^{−m}, 2p^{−m}) and the others below p^{−m}.

sources.locator: Proposition 2 and its proof, pp. 91–92
sources.match: Chooses the integral basis η_1, …, η_r of ℚ(η_1), the lexicographic sign change and the dominant real coordinates; the remark on p. 88 credits ideas of the Ferrero–Washington proof.

acceptance: For p = 3 or p = 5 (r = R) no sign change is needed.
For p = 7: R = 3, r = 2 and η_3 = η_1^3 = −1 = η_2 − η_1; replacing η_1 by −η_1 gives −1 = η_2 + (−η_1) with both coefficients positive, so j_0 = 3 and x_3 = x_1 + x_2 exceeds x_1 and x_2.

nodes.title: Washington's theorem on the non-p-part of class numbers
nodes.statement: Let k be a finite abelian extension of ℚ, p a prime, k_∞/k the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension with layers k_n, and ℓ ≠ p a prime. Then the exponent e_n(ℓ) of ℓ in h(k_n) is bounded independently of n; in fact it is constant for n large. (In the consumer's letters the tower prime is ℓ and the class-group prime is p.) This is a different theorem from Ferrero–Washington's μ = 0.
hypotheses: k abelian over ℚ; cyclotomic tower only (Washington exhibits non-cyclotomic ℤ_p-extensions where e_n(ℓ) is unbounded).
proofSteps: Reduce to the minus part and to p ≥ 3: for k imaginary, h_n = h_n^+h_n^- and it suffices that e_n^-(ℓ) is bounded; the case p = 2 and this reduction are Washington 1975 (Math. Ann. 214), cited on p. 88 and not read here (gap G-L4-W75).

Use the relative class number formula with characters χψ_n^j, ψ_n of conductor p^{n+1}, and the trace formula of Lemma 1 (pp. 89–90) expressing T_{n,m}(½ψ_n(α)^{−1}B_{1,χψ_n}) through p-adic digit sums s_{n−m}(αη), η in the sign-arranged representative set E.
Choose m_1 with all primes above ℓ inert in F_∞/F_{m_1}; a vanishing B_{1,χψ_n} mod a prime above ℓ for infinitely many n forces the trace congruence for all α.

Proposition 1 (statement p. 91, proof §4, pp. 95–97): for ℚ-independent β_j ∈ ℤ_p, given residues g_j mod d (p ∤ d), targets x_j and ε, for all large n some α ≡ 1 mod p^M has s_n(αβ_j) ≡ g_j mod d and |p^{−n−1}s_n(αβ_j) − x_j| < ε. The proof stores every finite digit pattern inside the expansions of a jointly normal family {γβ_j}; joint normality for almost every γ is Proposition 4 (p. 95), which Washington takes from Ferrero–Washington and which is the parent L4/fw-digit-equidistribution.

Case p ∤ f_χ (pp. 91–94): Proposition 2, with L4/torsion-root-sign-arrangement, gives α_1, α_2 whose digit sums agree except for η_0, where they differ by a carry; subtracting the two instances of Lemma 1 leaves −p^{n−m}ζ_0^{−1} ≢ 0 mod the prime above ℓ, contradicting the congruence.
Case p | f_χ (pp. 94–95): Proposition 3, the same construction with residues a and a − p modulo pd, leaves −χ(a − p)ζ_0^{−1}p^{n−m′}, nonzero because (a − p, pd) = 1.

sources.locator: Theorem, p. 87; §2 and Lemma 1, pp. 88–90; §3, Propositions 1–3 and the two cases, pp. 91–95; §4, proof of Proposition 1, pp. 95–97
sources.match: States and proves boundedness of the ℓ-part of h_n in the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension of an abelian field, ℓ ≠ p, for p ≥ 3, citing Washington 1975 for p = 2 and the reduction to the minus part.
